survey: A single wooden barrel standing upright on a plank deck, seen slightly from above at three-quarter view. The body is made of vertical staves that bulge at the middle and narrow toward the top and bottom, as a real cask does. Four dark iron hoops wrap it: one just below the top chime, two around the belly (one above and one below the bulge) and one at the base. Each hoop is a closed ring that follows the barrel's curve, with one rivet facing the camera. The top head is a flat disc of planks set into the rim of the stave ends, just below the top edge, which is where a real barrel head sits. The stave seams stay in roughly the same place from hoop to hoop, so the staves read as continuous boards. The bottom hoop and base sit flat on the deck, and a contact shadow falls behind and to the right, so the barrel is supported. There are no extra parts like a tap, bung glow or decorations.
